# Database Tools

> The MongoDB Database Tools are a collection of command-line utilities for working with a MongoDB deployment.

- [Database Tools Authentication](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/authentication.md): Learn how to use Atlas Workload Identity Federation with MongoDB Database Tools to authenticate connections on Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform.
- [bsondump](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump.md): Convert BSON files to human-readable formats like JSON using `bsondump`, a diagnostic tool for inspecting BSON files.
- [bsondump Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump/bsondump-compatibility-and-installation.md): Discover the compatibility and installation details for `bsondump`, including supported MongoDB server versions and platforms.
- [bsondump Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump/bsondump-examples.md): Explore examples of using `bsondump` to convert BSON files to JSON or produce debugging output.
- [The MongoDB Database Tools Documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/index.md): The MongoDB Database Tools are a collection of command-line utilities for working with a MongoDB deployment.
- [Install the MongoDB Database Tools](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/installation.md): Install the MongoDB Database Tools on Linux, macOS, or Windows using a package manager or downloaded archive, then verify the installation and explore common tasks.
- [Database Tools Logs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/logs.md): Learn how to manage and redirect logs from MongoDB Database Tools operations, including `mongoexport`, to stderr or a file.
- [``mongodump``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md): mongodump is a MongoDB database tool that creates a binary export of a database's contents to backup your data or migrate to a new deployment
- [mongodump Behavior, Access, and Usage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump/mongodump-behavior.md): Understand the behavior and usage of `mongodump`, including its limitations, access requirements, and role in backup strategies for MongoDB deployments.
- [mongodump Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump/mongodump-compatibility-and-installation.md): Install `mongodump` from the MongoDB Database Tools package, compatible with MongoDB Server and various platforms.
- [mongodump Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump/mongodump-examples.md): Explore mongodump examples for creating database backups, using access control, compressing output, and connecting to Atlas with AWS IAM credentials.
- [``mongoexport``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoexport.md): mongoexport is a database tool that produces a JSON or CSV export of data stored in a MongoDB instance.
- [mongoexport Behavior, Access, and Usage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoexport/mongoexport-behavior.md): Understand how `mongoexport` handles field names, type fidelity, and read preferences, and learn about the required access for using it.
- [mongoexport Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoexport/mongoexport-compatibility-and-installation.md): Discover the compatibility and installation details for `mongoexport`, including supported MongoDB server versions and platforms.
- [mongoexport Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoexport/mongoexport-examples.md): Explore examples of using `mongoexport` to export data from MongoDB in CSV or JSON format, including options for authentication and query filtering.
- [``mongofiles``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md): Use mongofiles to manipulate files in GridFS from the command line, supporting MongoDB versions with options for authentication and TLS/SSL configurations.
- [``mongoimport``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoimport.md): mongoimport is a MongoDB database tool that imports content from a JSON, CSV, or TSV file created by mongoexport or other tools.
- [mongoimport Behavior, Access, and Usage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoimport/mongoimport-behavior.md): Understand how `mongoimport` handles document field names, JSON formats, and other behaviors, including required access and write concern settings.
- [mongoimport Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoimport/mongoimport-compatibility-and-installation.md): Discover the compatibility and installation details for `mongoimport` version `100.10.0`, including supported MongoDB server versions and platforms.
- [mongoimport Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoimport/mongoimport-examples.md): Explore mongoimport examples for importing JSON and CSV data, including options for replacing, merging, and deleting documents, and connecting to remote hosts.
- [mongoimport Example Guide](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongoimport/mongoimport-guide.md): Details how to use `mongoimport` for importing JSON and CSV data.
- [``mongorestore``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md): mongorestore is a database tool that loads data from either a binary database dump created by mongodump or the standard input into a MongoDB instance.
- [mongorestore Behavior, Access, and Usage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-behavior-access-usage.md): Understand how to use `mongorestore` for restoring MongoDB data, including behavior, access requirements for self-managed and Atlas clusters, and usage in backup strategies.
- [mongorestore Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-compatibility-and-installation.md): Discover the compatibility and installation details for `mongorestore`, including supported MongoDB server versions and platforms.
- [mongorestore Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-examples.md): Explore examples of using `mongorestore` to restore MongoDB data, including restoring collections, using wildcards, and changing namespaces.
- [``mongostat``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md): Use mongostat to view the status of `mongod` or `mongos`instances and identify system bottlenecks with various options for connection and output customization.
- [mongostat Behavior, Access, and Usage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-behavior.md): Understand how to use `mongostat` with FIPS-compliant connections and required access privileges.
- [mongostat Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-compatibility-and-installation.md): Discover the compatibility and installation details for `mongostat`, including supported MongoDB server versions and platforms.
- [mongostat Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-examples.md): Explore using mongostat to monitor MongoDB performance, set collection periods, customize output fields, and connect to Atlas with AWS IAM credentials.
- [``mongotop``](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md): Track MongoDB instance read and write times per collection using `mongotop`, a command-line tool that provides statistics at configurable intervals.
- [mongotop Behavior, Access, and Usage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop/mongotop-behavior.md): Understand how `mongotop` collects and resets usage statistics, and the required access privileges for connecting to a `mongod` instance.
- [mongotop Compatibility and Installation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop/mongotop-compatibility-and-installation.md): Discover the compatibility and installation details for `mongotop`, including supported MongoDB server versions and platforms.
- [mongotop Examples](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop/mongotop-examples.md): Explore examples of using `mongotop` to monitor MongoDB performance, including connecting to Atlas clusters with AWS IAM credentials.
- [Database Tools Release Notes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/database-tools-changelog.md): Explore the release notes and changelogs for MongoDB Database Tools, covering new features, bug fixes, and security updates across all supported versions.
- [Database Tools 100.0.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.0.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.0.0, the first release with independent versioning from MongoDB Server, new command-line options, and bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.1.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.1.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes and bug fixes in Database Tools 100.1.0, including official support for MongoDB 4.4 and the new MONGODB-AWS authentication mechanism.
- [Database Tools 100.10.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.10.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.10.0, which adds support for MongoDB Server 8.0 and Ubuntu 24.04 platforms, with package updates and bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.11.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.11.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.11.0, which adds OIDC authentication for programmatic workloads along with dependency and maintenance updates.
- [Database Tools 100.12.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.12.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.12.0, which adds support for MongoDB Server 8.1 along with security updates, bug fixes, and maintenance releases.
- [Database Tools 100.13.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.13.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.13.0, which includes support for MongoDB Server 8.2 and Ubuntu 24.04, along with various updates and bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.14.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.14.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.14.0, which includes support for MongoDB Server 8.2, Ubuntu 24.04, and various updates and bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.15.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.15.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.15.0, which includes various updates and bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.16.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.16.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.16.0, which includes support for MongoDB Server 8.3 and the rawData CRUD API.
- [Database Tools 100.17.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.17.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.17.0, which adds build support for RedHat Enterprise Linux 10.
- [Database Tools 100.2.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.2.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes in Database Tools 100.2.0, including the deprecation of SSL flags in favor of tlsInsecure and new mongofiles put and get_regex subcommands.
- [Database Tools 100.3.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.3.0-changelog.md): Explore the Database Tools 100.3.0 changelog, which adds support for PKCS8-encrypted client private keys and secrets via a config file, plus bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.4.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.4.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes in Database Tools 100.4.0, including MongoDB Server 5.0 support, dump and restore of timeseries collections, and various bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.5.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.5.0-changelog.md): Explore the changelog for Database Tools 100.5.0, detailing build fixes, new platform support, and updates for compatibility with MongoDB Atlas Serverless.
- [Database Tools 100.6.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.6.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes and improvements in Database Tools 100.6.0, including an interactive SSL key password prompt for encrypted keys and various bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.7.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.7.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes and updates in Database Tools 100.7.0, which adds MongoDB 6.3 tests, Column Store Index tests, updated minimum Go version, and bug fixes.
- [Database Tools 100.8.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.8.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes and updates in Database Tools 100.8.0, which adds the tools to MongoDB Linux v7.0 repositories and includes associated dependency updates.
- [Database Tools 100.9.0 Changelogs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/release-notes/dbtools-100.9.0-changelog.md): Explore the changes in Database Tools 100.9.0, which adds support for MongoDB Server 7.0 along with bug fixes and platform compatibility improvements.
